newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easy, gilts in demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easy, gilts in demand.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday easier at 3.50-4.00 percent against opening levels of 5.00-5.50 percent on improved liquidity, dealers said.
They said liquidity with banks had improved following repurchase of securities by the Reserve Bank of India.

"There was an inflow of 41.94 billion rupees today on account of a reversal of a repos held on February 26," said a dealer. "Outflows were much less, only 10.5 billion towards the new repos auction on Saturday."
Dealers said they expected call money to remain easy through the rest of the week, given the current liquidity.
Prices of government securities rose in brisk trade on Monday, dealers said.
Securities worth 2.75 billion rupees were traded on the National Stock Exchange on Monday against the weekend figure of 2.11 billion rupees, dealers said.
"With call money easy, there is increased interest in securities," said a dealer.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock rose to 103.29 rupees from 103.25 and the 13.40 percent 1999 stock to 102.02 from 101.94, he said.
Three-month commercial paper was quoted at 12.5 percent and three-month certificates of deposit between 11.50 and 12.50 percent, dealers said.
